paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the God who arises is the same God who bends down low. In the very same song, He scatters His enemies like smoke, and He is "A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows" (Psalm 68:5). That's power AND tenderness in one breath. David isn't confused about who God is, and neither should you be.

So what does that mean for your Tuesday? David says God "daily bears our burden" (Psalm 68:19). DAILY, friend, so you don't have to carry it all by yourself. And when David says our God is a rescuer "from death" (Psalm 68:20), he's telling you the rescue goes all the way down, further than any problem on your list.

That's why David keeps calling for praise, even for all the kingdoms of the earth: "Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth" (Psalm 68:32). He closes by saying the God of Israel "gives strength and power to His people. Blessed be God!" (Psalm 68:35). So the right response is to join in. I can't carry a tune in a cookie tin, and I'm STILL singing! Trust the God who arises, lean on Him today, and sing it out.
